page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs, utilizing hyper-threading with 2.0 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 768.0 GB, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in several areas. The server achieved a PassMark CPU score of 93,126.45 and top-tier results in CPU extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only large block speeds reaching 506.7 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 207.77 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10%. Database operations are a strong point, with PassMark database operations scoring 35,335.9 and Redis SET operations reaching 122.52 million operations per second. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 87,583.29 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,410.0.

From a resource density perspective, the E96ds_v6 offers high memory and local storage density, making it qualitatively cost-effective for memory-bound and storage-intensive workloads. However, single-core performance represents a relative tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core performance and single-threaded compression/decompression benchmarks scoring in the average tier. LLM inference benchmarks show strong prompt processing speeds but average text generation speeds for large models. This hardware profile is suited for large-scale database systems, memory-cached applications like Redis, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8573C processor featuring 96 vCPUs running at 4.2 GHz, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. The server is configured with 768.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core memory ratio, and includes 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and large-block memory bandwidth. While single-core processing and text generation speeds represent moderate tradeoffs, its high memory density and multi-core capabilities make it highly suitable for large database deployments, in-memory caching, and intensive multi-threaded enterprise workloads.
